extracted.intended_audience: press, media and communications officers at universities, research institutes and other organisations (press officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for press officers on when and how to work with the Science Media Centre (SMC): submitting experts and briefings, expectations about contact/notifications, SMC services and limitations, and suitability of spokespeople. Focused on coordinating expert engagement with the news media via the SMC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing eligibility / types of stories SMC will work on
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do contact us if you think you have a story we could work together on, providing it falls into one of the following categories: Big, breaking science stories that are the headline news of the day; Controversial, messy, or politicised scientific issues; New scientific studies that may be sensationalised, overplayed or misrepresented; Issues where the scientific community wants to speak out as one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC can provide a neutral venue, act as a central coordination point, or support responses such as placing opinion pieces, briefing the press, or issuing third‑party expert quotes alongside press releases. If in doubt, contact SMC to discuss suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding scientists to the SMC database
rubrics_metrics.description: We are always on the lookout for top experts, but it’s important that each scientist and engineer knows us before we call them. So we generally don’t add experts before we’ve worked with them at least once – but we are happy for you to put them in touch with us for a quote or interview. If that goes well we can add them for future contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce experts via a quote or interview first; successful engagements make it appropriate to add them to SMC's contact database for future rapid contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding in breaking news
rubrics_metrics.description: When a story breaks we will usually email a large group to request quotes. But we can’t guarantee we’ll reach everyone! So the best advice is, don’t wait to hear from us; if you have an expert who can contribute usefully to the story, let us know!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on SMC emails during breaking events — proactively offer suitable experts to SMC as soon as possible to improve chances of media engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when SMC uses your experts
rubrics_metrics.description: We do our best to alert you every time we work with your experts, and we ask them to let you know too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect SMC to attempt to inform your press office when they engage your experts, but also ask your experts to notify you directly to ensure coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to contacting experts (direct contact preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most press officers are happy for their experts to be approached by us, and in all cases they have agreed to be contacted directly. We prefer it this way because we usually need to respond fast – we’re not trying to undermine you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not happy with direct contact, discuss arrangements with SMC, but bear in mind that time-sensitive stories require rapid access and delays can affect accuracy of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s just no way we can alert all press officers to every briefing they might find interesting and we often only have a few days’ notice. But when it’s something that concerns your institution or academics we’ll always try to keep you informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect comprehensive advance notice; be prepared for short lead times and maintain your own monitoring and communication with SMC where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speakers arrangement for briefings (news vs background)
rubrics_metrics.description: The briefings in your monthly report always have speakers already arranged – usually because it’s a news briefing with the authors of a paper presenting their work or another press officer has brought us the briefing fully formed. But for background briefings we like to have speakers from a variety of institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have an expert suitable for background/overview briefings, suggest them to SMC; such suggestions often lead to invitations. Understand that many news briefings will already have speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with SMC on controversial stories
rubrics_metrics.description: We specialise in controversial areas and we’re always keen to work on them. We are especially grateful for the tip-offs – e.g. work in publication that you expect to receive media attention of a particular type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC can assist with responses (breaking story handling, placing opinion pieces, briefing the press, spotlighting issues, issuing 3rd‑party expert quotes). Contact SMC even for background, advice or emotional support (catharsis).

rubrics_metrics.name: SMC training for scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t provide traditional media training, mainly because most universities and research councils already do. We run our Introduction to the News Media events, which are free and introduce inexperienced scientists and engineers to news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC provides introductory events for inexperienced researchers; expect institutions to provide more in‑depth media training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for press officers (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t offer any training for press officers but we would strongly recommend that you join Stempra, an informal network set up to bring together people working in science communication. They run events, training and an online forum to share questions and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For press officer professional development, use Stempra and other institutional training rather than expecting SMC to provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of PhD students as spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a PhD student doing some really interesting work – could we run a press briefing? Probably not! It might be interesting work with media appeal, but that’s not our remit. The most controversial headline subjects – climate change, GM, vaccines, animal research – generally demand more experienced experts from at least postdoc level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For high‑profile or controversial topics, expect SMC to seek experienced (postdoc or above) experts rather than junior researchers or PhD students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-scientist spokespeople / organisational comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Can we send you a comment from our spokesperson / manager / head of policy / head of comms? Usually not. It’s occasionally ok, under certain circumstances – for example if we’re seeking quotes on a much broader story where there is room for lots of voices from the scientific community. But in general it is only scientists/engineers we want for quotes on research papers and breaking news – so best to check with us first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer scientist/engineer voices for research and breaking news; organisational spokespeople are generally unsuitable except in limited, broader contexts — check with SMC beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMC policy on press releases and journalist lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you send out a press release for us, or share your journalist lists with us? No, we don’t send out press releases as we can’t do other organisations’ PR. We also do not share our journalist lists, but we do notify you about specialist journalists moving jobs etc. in our monthly report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect SMC to perform your organisation's PR or to disclose their media contact lists; they may provide limited informational updates (e.g., journalist moves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct titling / affiliation of experts
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t want to get this wrong and we know how important it is for your organisations to have names reported correctly. But many experts represent multiple institutions, so we ask the expert how he/she wants to be billed. If you want someone’s affiliation changed in this way, please copy in the expert when you let us know so we can get their direct permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the expert when requesting changes to billing/affiliation to obtain their direct permission and avoid misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact SMC
rubrics_metrics.description: If you or your experts need the SMC’s help, you can contact us on: t: +44 (0)20 7611 8300 e: smc@sciencemediacentre.org
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear contact details for rapid engagement; the FAQs are also available as a PDF for offline reference.
